$comment: 01.7.1-T2 / DECISIONS §4 / 00 §5.7 S6. The single licence allow/deny list consumed by scripts/licence-scan.sh for BOTH ecosystems (npm via license-checker-rseidelsohn, NuGet via nuget-license). Evaluation: every licence token of every dependency is classified — first matching verdict wins in deny > warn > allow > unknown order; 'unknown' means 'no allow pattern matched' and behaves like warn. deny/warn verdicts fail the gate UNLESS the package is listed under an exception keyed by an ADR id; a warn-level exception still prints the warning (that is the 'warn + required ADR row' rule for LGPL). SPDX 'OR' expressions are treated conservatively: a denied token anywhere in the expression denies the package — choose the permitted side by adding an ADR exception. Exceptions carry package keys as '<ecosystem>:<name>' or '<ecosystem>:<name>@<version>' where ecosystem is npm|nuget; the exception does not apply until the ADR id exists in docs/adr/.

deny.why: Business Source License — commercial use restricted until change date
ELv2 forbids providing as managed service
end-user licence agreements are not open licences

warn.why: LGPL needs an ADR row (DECISIONS §4; Hangfire precedent in ADR-0002)
strong copyleft — needs an ADR row (AGPL/LGPL are already classified above)
Mozilla Public License — weak copyleft, needs an ADR row
Eclipse Public License — weak copyleft, needs an ADR row
licence text cannot be machine-classified — needs an ADR row
unlicensed third-party code has no usable licence

ADR-0002.reason: MPL-2.0 weak copyleft is compatible with closed-source SaaS: lightningcss is a build-time-only transitive of vite (via vitest) and never ships in runtime artefacts; ADR-0002's vitest row carries the direct dependency. axe-core is a test-time-only devDependency of apps/web (a11y specs in jsdom), unmodified and never bundled; its own ADR-0002 row carries it (09.1.1-T7). Package keys are case-insensitive fnmatch patterns ('ecosystem:name' or 'ecosystem:name@version').
